reason: Tells the learner to sort by the property lost rather than the tool used, and warns that one technology (encryption) can be a control or a weapon. That defuses the 'encryption = confidentiality' reflex on the ransomware item.

It offers two tests (the loss noticed first, the loss suffered unknowingly) but never says which one decides. A learner can read the 'hidden' loss as the real one and put ransomware under Confidentiality (data may have been exfiltrated too). The silent-alteration items gain nothing from it either.

Gives each bucket a working definition (who someone is / action undeniable afterwards / holding less data) and frames the test as purpose. A learner unsure what non-repudiation means can act on it. Small caveat: 'in the first place' fits data minimisation better than erasure.

'Sort by the reason the measure was put there' repeats hint 0's 'what each measure exists for' and the prompt's 'primarily provides'. It names no item and no distinction (e.g. a signature also authenticates), so it adds no method.

Supplies a concrete test (what does the enforcing: a machine, a rule people follow, or a physical barrier) that settles the locked-door, encryption and background-check items without relying on the bucket labels.
The prompt already says 'Ignore when it acts; that is its function, not its type.' This hint repeats that and adds nothing usable.

The prompt already glosses each canon (public safety, your own honesty, the client, the profession). The hint recasts that same gloss as 'who is protected' without a way to separate close cases, such as an unauthorised scan (II vs III) or the medical-device vendor (I vs II).
The prompt already says 'most directly about one canon' and warns that ranking is not classification. 'Ask which it is fundamentally about' is the same instruction again, with no test.

It describes the inside of a single step ('Assess likelihood x impact and rank it') and says nothing about where that step sits among the others. The key Identify-before-Assess relation is not touched, so it is a tautology that costs quality.

It establishes that residual-risk documentation and acceptance come after treatment, which fixes the tail of the sequence. It could be sharper by saying residual risk is known only after the control is applied and verified.

The decision path is useful, but it offers only 'states an intention' for Policy. 'Every system must have a named owner who is accountable' reads as a specific requirement, so the hint steers it toward Standard. Policies also assign roles and accountability, and the hint misses that.
Separating force from specificity is a real method. It stops the detailed-but-optional passphrase advice going to Standard, and it lets a mandatory but high-level statement land in Policy.
